perspective:
From Mason Hurley’s perspective, he has access to the following:

- Mason is an accountant at a small community center. Martha Moua is a personal care aide there. They are colleagues but not personally close; they interact mainly through work.
- While reviewing financial reports, Mason noticed discrepancies and suspected Martha might be mismanaging funds. He felt suspicious and anxious. He asked Martha to discuss the report, saying the numbers did not add up.
- He heard Martha agree to discuss it, say there was likely a reasonable explanation, and ask which discrepancies he meant. Mason pointed to unusually high healthcare expenses that did not match usual spending. He heard Martha say there may have been a misentry and that she would review and correct errors.
- After further review, Mason concluded the discrepancies were due to a simple clerical error, not mismanagement. He felt relieved but embarrassed about his initial suspicion.
- He told Martha he appreciated her quick clarification and that it seemed to be a clerical error. He heard Martha say errors happen and she was glad they cleared it up. Mason apologized for suspecting her and said he should have asked first. He heard Martha say it was okay, that she understood he was being thorough, and that they should double-check entries next time.
- Mason now believes Martha is competent, but he believes the financial management system is inadequate because of recurring clerical errors. He feels frustrated with the system and empathetic toward Martha.
- He told Martha the issue is not her management but the current system. He proposed a new, more robust financial system, said he would draft a proposal, and asked for her input. He heard Martha agree, ask what he suggested, call it a great idea, offer to help, and say it should address the gaps they identified.
- Mason drafted the proposal and felt hopeful but uncertain whether management would approve and implement it.
- He told Martha he finished the draft, believed it would benefit operations, and was unsure how management would receive it. He heard Martha call it solid, encourage confidence, say the benefits were clear and hard to argue against, and agree to help gather data. Mason planned a detailed presentation and asked Martha to help gather data.
- After presenting the new financial system proposal to management, Mason felt satisfied with his effort but physically and mentally exhausted. He believed he had done everything possible to advocate for it.
- He told Martha the presentation went well and it was now up to management. He heard Martha praise his work, suggest taking time off, say he deserved a break, and tell him to enjoy his break and let her know if he needed anything. Mason decided to take a few days off to recharge and reflect, hoping for good news.
